These kernels do no math, so they are pure removable overhead; the small shape (2x256x64x64) only reaches 1.0106x because the two shape-independent weight copies are a fixed tax on a 0.363 ms forward. That a tiled transpose is the right shape here is shown by our existing `norm_silu_res_t_kernel`, whose 32x33-tile transpose hits gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak = 89.52% with the SOL rule stating it is 'utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance' — near roofline, whereas a TensorIterator transpose copy pays sector amplification on its strided side. strategy.optimisation method: Split the batch into 2 independent chunks (GroupNorm groups are per-sample, so this is exact) and software-pipeline them across two CUDA streams with events, so each chunk's memory-bound GroupNorm/SiLU/transpose epilogue overlaps the other chunk's compute-bound conv. Convs stay ordered on the main stream.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Declare it in _CPP_SRC and add to the `functions=[...]` list. Keep all existing kernels unchanged.
2. `ModelNew.__init__`: create one reusable side stream `self._side = torch.cuda.Stream()` (created once, never per call).
3. forward: after `res`/B,C,H,W/P are computed, do the two weight transforms (`w1`,`w2`) first on the current stream (hoisted out of any loop), then allocate `out = torch.empty_like(res)` and set `nchunk = 2 if B >= 2 else 1`; chunk bounds `a_i = i*B//nchunk, b_i = (i+1)*B//nchunk`. Slices `res[a:b]`, `out[a:b]` of a contiguous NCHW tensor are contiguous, so they can be passed straight to the extension.
4. MILESTONE (must compile and match): implement the chunked pipeline on ONE stream first — for each chunk run `to_nhwc(res[a:b])` -> conv1 -> `gn_silu_nhwc` -> conv2 -> `gn_silu_res_nchw_out(..., out[a:b], ...)` with the per-chunk batch size `b-a` passed as B. When nchunk==1 this must be byte-identical to today's path (protects the 1x256x131x131 shape). Verify numerics, then proceed.
5. Add the side stream: `main = torch.cuda.current_stream(); s = self._side; s.wait_stream(main)`. Inside `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` run `xn[i] = _ext.to_nhwc(res[a_i:b_i])` for all chunks, recording `ev_t[i]` (torch.cuda.Event) immediately after each.

This makes chunk0's GroupNorm overlap chunk1's conv1.
7. Second loop, same shape: on main `main.wait_event(ev_e[i])`, `o2[i]=F.conv2d(g1[i],w2,None,1,1)`, `ev_b[i].record(main)`; on s `s.wait_event(ev_b[i])`, `_ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(o2[i], res[a_i:b_i], out[a_i:b_i], norm2..., eps, 32, b_i-a_i, C, P)`, `ev_f[i].record(s)`.

Allocator safety (required, not optional): call `.record_stream(s)` on every tensor allocated on main but consumed on s (`o1[i]`, `o2[i]`, `res`) and `.record_stream(main)` on every tensor allocated on s but consumed on main (`xn[i]`, `g1[i]`), plus `out.record_stream(s)` since s writes a main-stream allocation.

strategy.optimisation method: Capture the entire ModelNew.forward (2 cuDNN convs + 2 weight layout copies + our 6 custom-kernel launches) into one torch.cuda.CUDAGraph and replay it, binding the caller's live input tensors by address instead of copying into static input buffers, so no extra DRAM traffic is added.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Refactor only: move the current body of `ModelNew.forward` verbatim into `def _forward_impl(self, x, conv1_weight, norm1_weight, norm1_bias, conv2_weight, norm2_weight, norm2_bias, eps)` returning `out`; make `forward` call it. No CUDA source, kernel, or launch-shape change anywhere. THIS IS THE FIRST COMPILABLE/CORRECT MILESTONE — validate all 4 shapes here.
2. Add state in `__init__`: `self._graphs = {}` (key -> (graph, out_tensor)), `self._seen = {}` (key -> int), `self._graph_disabled = False`.
3. Add `_sig(self, tensors, eps)` returning a hashable tuple: for each of the 7 tensors `(t.data_ptr(), tuple(t.shape), tuple(t.stride()), t.dtype)`, plus `float(eps)`. Rationale: a CUDA graph binds ADDRESSES, not data, so replay reads whatever bytes currently live at those addresses; equal (ptr, shape, stride, dtype) therefore guarantees a correct result with zero copy-in.
4. In `forward`: if `self._graph_disabled`, or any tensor is not CUDA/float32/contiguous-as-expected, or any `requires_grad` is True, or `torch.is_grad_enabled()` and any input requires grad -> return `self._forward_impl(...)` (eager fallback).
5. Compute `key = self._sig(...)`. If `key in self._graphs`: `g, out = self._graphs[key]; g.replay(); return out`. Return the static `out` directly — do NOT clone it (a clone is a 67 MB copy ≈ 90 us on the mid shape and would erase the gain).
6. Else `self._seen[key] = self._seen.get(key,0)+1`; if count < 3, run and return `self._forward_impl(...)` eagerly. This warms cuDNN algo selection and the caching allocator before capture.
7. On the 3rd sighting, capture inside `try/except Exception`: create `s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())`; inside `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` run `self._forward_impl(...)` twice under `torch.no_grad()`; then `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize()`.
8. Then `g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()`; `with torch.no_grad(), torch.cuda.graph(g): out = self._forward_impl(x, conv1_weight, ..., eps)` — pass the caller's ORIGINAL tensors so their addresses are baked in. `torch.cuda.synchronize()`.
9. Store `self._graphs[key] = (g, out)`, then call `g.replay()` once before returning `out` (capture itself executes nothing, so `out` is otherwise undefined).
10. On any exception during 7-9 set `self._graph_disabled = True` and return `self._forward_impl(...)`.
11. Bound memory: if `len(self._graphs) > 8`, clear `self._graphs` and `self._seen` before capturing (each graph holds a private pool containing the conv/intermediate buffers; the 4x256x256x256 shape alone holds ~1.3 GB).
12. Do NOT allocate static input buffers and do NOT `copy_` inputs anywhere — that would add a full read+write of the 67 MB activation per call. Do NOT move tensors across devices.
13. Validate: for each of the 4 benchmark shapes call `ModelNew.forward` at least 6 times (so calls 1-2 are eager, 3 captures, 4-6 replay) and compare every call against the reference at atol 0.0028; then allocate a fresh, differently-valued input set and verify the result is still correct (new key -> eager, then new capture).

The same 15 launches serve the 2x256x64x64 shape whose GPU work is ~1/8 as large (~0.28 ms), so the fixed gap is ~23% there, which is exactly why that shape scores only 1.0106x while the mid shape reaches 1.0769x. strategy.bottleneck: gn_partial_kernel reads the conv output with a channel-strided, split-16B pattern: each thread grabs only its group's 8 channels (32B) while neighbours are 1KB apart, so it sustains just 63% of DRAM peak (vs 86-89% for every other memory kernel) and burns 140us/forward (6% of total).
strategy.optimisation method: Rewrite the GroupNorm statistics pass so a warp reads 32 consecutive float4s (512B contiguous) of one pixel row, covering all 32 groups at once, with the per-group partial sums folded by an in-warp pair shuffle plus a small 8x32 shared accumulator, instead of one block per (n,group) walking strided pixels.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep every other mechanism untouched: nchw_to_nhwc_kernel, norm_silu_res_t_kernel, norm_silu_nhwc_kernel, gn_finalize_kernel, weight_to_nhwc and the forward() call sequence are unmodified; the round-1 tiled-transpose path must remain in use.
2. Add a new kernel `gn_partial_c256_kernel(const float4* __restrict__ in4, float2* __restrict__ partial, int P, int nparts, int pixPerPart)` specialised for C==256, G==32, CPG==8 (all compile-time constants of this problem: 64 float4 per pixel row, group = float4index>>1).
3. Launch shape: `dim3 grid(nparts, B)`, block 256 threads. blockIdx.y = n, blockIdx.x = part; p0 = part*pixPerPart, p1 = min(p0+pixPerPart, P).
4. Thread mapping inside the kernel: `int c4 = threadIdx.x & 63;` (float4 column, 0..63) and `int r = threadIdx.x >> 6;` (0..3, row offset). A warp therefore spans 32 consecutive c4 values => one 512B contiguous load per instruction (this is the whole point; do NOT map threads to pixels).
5. Loop: `for (int p = p0 + r; p < p1; p += 4) { float4 v = in4[((long long)n*P + p)*64 + c4]; s += v.x+v.y+v.z+v.w; sq += v.x*v.x+v.y*v.y+v.z*v.z+v.w*v.w; }` with s, sq as two float registers only.
6. Per-thread group is fixed: `int g = c4 >> 1;` Lanes l and l^1 of a warp share g, so fold with `s += __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, s, 1);` and the same for sq.
7. Block fold without atomics: `__shared__ float ss[8][32], ssq[8][32];` zero-initialise all 8*32 entries (each thread clears one slot of each array), `__syncthreads()`, then every even lane writes `ss[warpId][g]=s; ssq[warpId][g]=sq;` (warpId = threadIdx.x>>5, 8 warps, each covering 16 of the 32 groups), `__syncthreads()`.
8. Write-out: threads 0..31 (index g) sum the 8 warp rows and store `partial[((long long)(n*32+g))*nparts + part] = make_float2(sum_s, sum_sq);` — exactly the layout gn_finalize already expects, so gn_finalize is unchanged.
9. Host side in compute_scale_shift: when (C==256 && G==32) choose `nparts = max(1, min((1024 + B - 1)/B, (P+3)/4)); pixPerPart = (P + nparts - 1)/nparts; nparts = (P + pixPerPart - 1)/pixPerPart;` allocate `partial` as {B*G*nparts, 2} floats and launch the new kernel with grid(nparts, B), 256 threads. Pass the same nparts to gn_finalize.
10. Otherwise fall back to the existing gn_partial_kernel and its current nparts computation, so any non-256-channel case stays correct.
11. Guards: the p<p1 bound in the loop covers odd P (131*131=17161); the float4 cast is safe because C*4=1024B and torch allocations are 256B-aligned.
12. Verify all four shapes against the reference (atol 0.0028), then profile gn_partial's dram throughput.
strategy.evidence: Numbers: gn_partial gpu__dram_throughput = 63.0% while norm_silu_nhwc = 86.58%, norm_silu_res_t = 89.21%, nchw_to_nhwc = 86.85% — it is the only memory kernel with headroom; its 70.1us x2 launches = 140us of the 2292us forward (6.1%). Bytes moved = 0.63*1.792TB/s*70.1us = 79MB for a 67MB tensor, i.e. ~18% DRAM over-fetch, and l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate 47.04% shows half of its accesses are the second 16B float4 of the same 32B line being re-requested (the `ptr[j]` loop over CPG). Section analysis (SourceCounters/UncoalescedGlobalAccess) states 2,097,152 excessive sectors = 50% of 4,195,328 total, pointing at exactly this strided `base + p*C + g*CPG` read. Ruled out as #1: occupancy/registers — achieved occupancy 101.15%, sm__warps_active 95.55% of peak, 37 regs/thread, 0 local-spill requests, so no launch-shape or register fix applies; compute is also ruled out at sm__throughput 3.18%. History: Previous Attempt #1 (stream pipelining) is case (a) — the deciding numbers are that the rejected profile's kernels are unchanged (gn_partial 73.2us vs 70.1us, identical grids, norm_silu_res_t dram 89.41% vs 89.21%), i.e. both phases were already at their own roof (conv ~86% of TF32 peak, epilogues 86-89% of DRAM) so overlapping them had no slack to harvest; that direction is dead and I instead delete wasted bytes. Method chosen outside allowed_methods: CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers would require copying a 67MB static input per call (~78us, +3.4%) against ~15 launches of overhead, a guaranteed regression on the two large shapes. Delta vs the round-1 Improve_Coalescing win: that one added shared-memory 32x33 tiled transposes for the three layout copies; this one touches a kernel round 1 never modified (gn_partial), uses no shared-memory tile and no transpose, and changes the thread->data mapping from one-block-per-(n,group) strided-pixel to one-block-per-(n,pixel-chunk) covering all 32 groups with a pair shuffle.

strategy.bottleneck: Layout conversion, not math. PyTorch's generic elementwise kernel converting x (and both weights) to channels_last costs 11.2% of steady GPU time, and gn_partial wastes 50% of its sectors (DRAM only 62.41% of peak) from a 1KB-stride per-thread NHWC access.
strategy.optimisation method: Own every NCHW->NHWC conversion with shared-memory tiled transpose kernels (activation + both weights in one launch), and re-index gn_partial so consecutive threads cover one full 32B sector of a group instead of one pixel each. Pure coalescing/transaction-size work; CUDA-graph capture untouched.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Add `nchw_to_nhwc_kernel(const float* in, float* out, int P, int C)`: `__shared__ float tile[32][33];` block (32,8), grid ((P+63)/64, (C+31)/32, B). Loop t=0,1 with p0=blockIdx.x*64+t*32, c0=blockIdx.y*32, n=blockIdx.z. Load phase: p=p0+tx, for k=0,8,16,24: c=c0+ty+k; if(p<P&&c<C) tile[ty+k][tx]=in[((long long)n*C+c)*P+p]; `__syncthreads()`. Store phase: c=c0+tx, for k=0,8,16,24: pp=p0+ty+k; if(pp<P&&c<C) out[((long long)n*P+pp)*C+c]=tile[tx][ty+k]; `__syncthreads()` before next t.

strategy.bottleneck: gn_partial_kernel is the only streaming pass far from bandwidth: 61.0% DRAM vs 86.9-89.5% for the other full-tensor kernels, 87.5% long-scoreboard stall. Its per-(n,group) 32B-stripe indexing issues 16 scattered sectors per warp request instead of one contiguous 512B request.
strategy.optimisation method: Refine the existing coalescing mechanism in gn_partial: re-map blocks from (pixel-chunk, n*G) to (pixel-chunk, n) so one block sums ALL 32 groups of a pixel range, letting consecutive threads read consecutive float4s (512B contiguous per warp) with one fixed group accumulator per thread.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep every existing mechanism intact: CUDA-graph capture/replay, the NHWC transpose kernels, weights_to_nhwc, norm_silu_nhwc, norm_silu_res_t and gn_finalize are NOT touched; only gn_partial and its launch config change.
2. Add a new kernel next to the old one (old kept as fallback):
   `__global__ void gn_partial_pix_kernel(const float* __restrict__ in, float2* __restrict__ partial, int P, int C, int CPG, int G, int nparts, int pixPerPart)` with block = 256 threads, grid = dim3(nparts, B) (blockIdx.y = n, blockIdx.x = part).
3. Index math inside it: `int n=blockIdx.y, part=blockIdx.x; int p0=part*pixPerPart; int p1=min(p0+pixPerPart,P); int vecC=C>>2; int vpg=CPG>>2; int tid=threadIdx.x; int j=tid%vecC; int row=tid/vecC; const float4* base=reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(in)+ (long long)n*P*vecC;` (base is 16B-aligned because n*P*C*4 is a multiple of 16).
4. Accumulation loop (vector width stays float4, never scalarised): `float s=0,sq=0; for(int p=p0+row;p<p1;p+=(256/vecC)){ float4 t=base[(long long)p*vecC + j]; s+=t.x+t.y+t.z+t.w; sq+=t.x*t.x+t.y*t.y+t.z*t.z+t.w*t.w; }`. With C=256, vecC=64, so lanes 0-31 of a warp read 32 consecutive float4 = one contiguous 512B region; the row split (4 rows) handles 4 pixels per iteration. Tail pixels are handled by the `p<p1` guard (works for odd P such as 131*131).
5. Two-stage shared reduction (each thread owns exactly ONE group, g = j/vpg): `__shared__ float2 sm[256]; sm[tid]=make_float2(s,sq); __syncthreads(); if(tid<vecC){ float2 a=sm[tid]; for(int r=1;r<256/vecC;++r){ float2 b=sm[tid+r*vecC]; a.x+=b.x; a.y+=b.y;} sm[tid]=a;} __syncthreads(); if(tid<G){ float2 a=make_float2(0,0); for(int k=0;k<vpg;++k){ float2 b=sm[tid*vpg+k]; a.x+=b.x; a.y+=b.y;} partial[((long long)(n*G+tid))*nparts+part]=a; }`. This preserves the existing partial layout `[bg*nparts+part]` so gn_finalize_kernel and its grid (B*G blocks) stay unchanged.
6. Host wiring in compute_scale_shift: if `(C%4==0 && CPG%4==0 && (C/4)<=256 && 256%(C/4)==0)` use the new path with `int nparts=(2048+B-1)/B; int maxparts=P/8; if(maxparts<1)maxparts=1; if(nparts>maxparts)nparts=maxparts; if(nparts<1)nparts=1; int pixPerPart=(P+nparts-1)/nparts; nparts=(P+pixPerPart-1)/pixPerPart;`, allocate partial as {B*G*nparts,2}, launch `gn_partial_pix_kernel<<<dim3(nparts,B),256>>>`; otherwise keep the old kernel and old nparts formula verbatim.
7. Verify correctness on all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) before any tuning; only then re-profile.
8. Do NOT change block size away from 256 (it must stay a multiple of vecC=64) and do not add extra global buffers beyond the (still tiny) partial tensor, so graph capture keeps working with a static launch sequence.
strategy.evidence: Metrics: gn_partial_kernel gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak = 61.03 while norm_silu_res_t = 89.53 and norm_silu_nhwc = 86.85 on the same 67MB tensors; gn_partial l1tex__throughput = 10.08% and smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard = 87.46% with duration 73.12us x2 launches = ~146us of the ~2248us NCU-summed forward (6.5%), i.e. it moves 67MB at ~0.92TB/s vs the 1.53-1.58TB/s the other kernels achieve. Section analysis for gn_partial: SOLBottleneck OPT 'low compute throughput and memory bandwidth utilization ... below 60.0% of peak typically indicate latency issues' and CPIStall 'each warp spends 121.0 cycles stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on a L1TEX operation'. Ruled out (secondary): occupancy/compute are NOT the limit - achieved occupancy 116.37% (55.86 active warps/SM, theoretical 100%) and sm__throughput = 8.53%, so more warps or cheaper math cannot help; the cost is the scattered request shape of `base + p*C + j*4` in gn_partial_kernel, where a warp touches 16 different pixels 1024B apart. Previous attempt (kernel_20260911_091625, scored 1.1112, rejected): its gn_partial stayed at 60.19% DRAM / 74.24us, i.e. the inefficiency did not move at all -> failure class (b), the mechanism never engaged on this kernel; my plan attacks it directly and differently. History/de-dup: this refines the base's round-5 'Improve_Coalescing_and_TransactionSize' (which introduced the sector-pair indexing inside gn_partial); concrete delta vs that round: block mapping changes from one block per (n,group) reading a 32B stripe to one block per (n,pixel-chunk) reading all 32 groups (full 1024B per pixel), each thread keeps ONE fixed group accumulator, and the block reduction becomes a two-stage shared-memory row/pair reduction instead of the warp-shuffle block_reduce2. Method note: the only allowed method (CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers) is already implemented in the base (round 3) and cannot be applied again; the measured gap is a memory-access-pattern gap, so I select the coalescing method and compose with, rather than replace, the graph mechanism.
strategy.expected_metric_change: gn_partial gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct 61.03 -> >80; smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard 87.46% -> <70%; l1tex__throughput 10.08% -> higher (fewer wavefronts per request); gn_partial duration 73.1us -> ~45-50us per launch (~2.5% end-to-end). Anti-regression: registers/thread must not exceed 40 (per-thread state drops to 2 float accumulators), shared memory 2KB/block must keep >=8 blocks/SM so achieved occupancy stays >=100%, and no vector load may be replaced by scalar lanes. Mechanisms that must stay alive and would reveal a loss if broken: total kernel launch count per forward must stay 8 (graph capture still engaging - if it fell back the launch count/host time would rise), the NHWC path and channels_last cuDNN engine selection must be unchanged (conv kernel name must remain cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop_optimized_tf32 with the same ~840us/conv), and norm_silu_nhwc / norm_silu_res_t DRAM% must stay >=86%.
